subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Wisdom of Crowds
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Wisdom of Crowds.

hook.text: In 1906, Galton asked a crowd to guess an ox's weight. The average guess was off by one pound. No expert came close.

buildup.text: Surowiecki showed that diverse, independent guesses aggregated together outperform individual experts on many problems.

discovery.text: Three conditions are needed: diversity of opinion, independence of judgment, and a good method to aggregate the answers.

twist.text: Social influence destroys crowd wisdom. Let people see each other's guesses and they converge on a single wrong answer.

climax.text: Prediction markets work because they aggregate independent bets. Discussion forums fail because opinions cluster.

punchline.text: Crowds are wise only if each person thinks alone first.

quiz.question: What destroys the wisdom of crowds?
options: Allowing people to see each other's answers before guessing

details.summary: The wisdom of crowds phenomenon shows that large groups of independent thinkers often produce more accurate estimates than individual experts. Averaging many diverse, independent guesses cancels out individual errors, yielding surprisingly precise collective judgments.
details.whyItMatters: Crowd wisdom underpins prediction markets, democratic decision making, and decentralized systems. Understanding when crowds are wise and when they fail helps design better information aggregation systems for business and policy.
takeaways: Independent diverse estimates average to remarkable accuracy
Crowd wisdom requires independence, diversity, and decentralization
Social influence destroys crowd wisdom by reducing opinion diversity

faq.question: When does the wisdom of crowds fail?
faq.answer: Crowds fail when they lack independence: social influence, groupthink, and information cascades make individual estimates correlated rather than independent. When everyone copies the same source, the crowd becomes no wiser than that single source.

faq.question: How do prediction markets use crowd wisdom?
faq.answer: Prediction markets let participants bet real money on outcomes. Prices aggregate diverse private information from thousands of independent bettors. These markets consistently outperform expert forecasts for elections, sports, and business events.
